github_issue.notes: Every factual claim checks out against the repo: the endpoint at registry/api/system_routes.py:333-354 does call the raw cascade, _detect_cloud_from_env (telemetry.py:62-70) returns aws on AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, .env.example:515 ships AWS_REGION=us-east-1 (and docker-compose.yml:119 even defaults it), _resolve_cloud (telemetry.py:317-341) applies explicit-override-then-hint-then-cascade exactly as stated, and the config.py:784-807 validator lists the exact allowed values. Acceptance criteria are all testable (endpoint JSON per branch, schema unchanged, 401 preserved, no frontend change) and out-of-scope items are named with rationale. Strongest aspect is the verified root-cause chain including the collector allowlist (terraform/telemetry-collector/lambda/collector/schemas.py accepts explicit/operator_declared/operator_declined); the only unverifiable claims are the upstream issue #1306 link and the operator-experience label's existence in the repo.

lld.notes: The design is grounded in the real repo at unusual precision: endpoint lines 333-354, _resolve_cloud at telemetry.py:317-341, the lru_cache on the cascade at line 218, the 60s hint cache, registry_routes.py:734 as the existing _resolve_cloud caller, and the existing 401 test at tests/unit/test_stats_endpoint.py:450-458 all match the source, and the drop-in handler code is exactly right for an already-async endpoint. The compatibility argument is structural (unset path literally re-invokes the same cached cascade), and alternatives are genuinely evaluated. The one concrete error is Step 2's claim that patching _detect_cloud_from_env makes the fallthrough test hermetic regardless of host env: _detect_cloud_provider_with_method is functools.lru_cache'd, so a cache populated earlier in the same pytest process (e.g. by tests/unit/core/test_telemetry.py::test_no_pii_in_startup_payload, which reaches the real cascade) bypasses the patch — the repo's own tests/unit/core/test_cloud_detection.py uses an autouse cache_clear fixture for exactly this, and the LLD does not.

review.notes: This is a real review, not praise theater: it disagrees with its own LLD, adds a missing hint-branch test and a source-of-truth call-site comment, and verifies the Prometheus label question against the collector allowlist — findings that materially improved the design and are visible in the revised LLD and patch. The frontend wording observation is genuine (UptimeDisplay.tsx title is literally 'Detected via ${method}'). Two deductions: the Backend reviewer's 'must-fix' rationale is partly wrong — the override-set test cannot construct a repository because _resolve_cloud returns on the explicit branch before _get_operator_cloud_hint is ever awaited (telemetry.py:328-331), so stubbing there is harmless defense, not a necessity — and none of the five reviewers caught the lru_cache test-isolation hazard in the very patch-target analysis the review explicitly endorses.

testing.notes: The plan has real oracles at every level: exact expected JSON per branch (on_premises/explicit, aws/env, unknown/operator_declined — all matching _resolve_cloud semantics), the exact existing 401 test it must not break (verified at tests/unit/test_stats_endpoint.py:450), a working pytest command, a compose verification against the real 'registry' service, and a three-surface consistency scenario tying endpoint, log line, and tooltip. Deployment wiring is correctly marked N/A since no config changes. The weaknesses: the shipped fallthrough unit test asserts aws/env while _detect_cloud_provider_with_method is process-lifetime lru_cache'd, so on any full-suite run where an earlier test in the same process (e.g. test_no_pii_in_startup_payload) populated the cache, the patched _detect_cloud_from_env never executes and the assertion fails — the plan claims hermeticity it does not have. The .oauth-tokens/ingress.json token path is also unverified (repo e2e tests use admin-bot-token.json).

implementation.notes: The patch is real and correct: it applies cleanly (verified with git apply --check against the checked-out baseline dbaa153, which matches the stated baseline), the production change swaps the in-handler import to _resolve_cloud with await in the already-async handler exactly as designed, the docstring now lists the true label set, auth is untouched, and the summary's +17/-8 and +104 line counts are accurate. The strict-markers deviation note is honest and verified (pyproject.toml:105 enables --strict-markers and 'api' is absent from the marker list at lines 126-137). The largest defect is in the new test class: test_override_unset_falls_back_to_detection_cascade ignores the cascade's functools.lru_cache — if any earlier test in the same pytest process ran the real cascade, the patched _detect_cloud_from_env is bypassed and the aws/env assertion becomes order- and host-dependent, contradicting the repo's own cache_clear convention in tests/unit/core/test_cloud_detection.py; run in isolation (as testing.md prescribes) it passes, so the flaw surfaces only at suite scope.

verdict: Excellent, repository-verified work across all five artifacts with the single material limitation being a shared blind spot: the new override-unset regression test ignores the process-lifetime lru_cache on _detect_cloud_provider_with_method, making it order- and host-dependent under a full-suite run even though the production change itself is exactly right.
